# Fun / Creative Add‑Ins (Old‑School MySpace Style)

Think in terms of “dress‑up” rather than “build‑out” – little flourishes that
don’t change the gallery’s purpose but give visitors something to poke at.

- Animated or randomly‑switching backgrounds – gradients that slowly cycle,
  looping GIFs behind the content, a parallax starfield.
- A “guest‑book” or shout‑box where people can leave a short message that
  appears as a floating speech‑bubble or sticky note.
- An auto‑playing (and toggleable) MIDI/8‑bit/lo‑fi playlist in the corner –
  a tiny player styled like an old Winamp skin.
- Secret “easter eggs” – click an innocuous icon and a pixelated cat walks
  across the screen, or confetti bursts from the header.
- Profile‑style badges/achievements: “first visit”, “loved 10 pieces”, “found
  the hidden link” that light up on a visitor’s sidebar.
- A marquee or animated “About me” block in Comic Sans with glitter text that
  scrolls across.
- A cursor trail of sparkles, or a custom cursor that changes when you hover
  over certain art.
- A little “scrapbook” area where users can drag‑and‑drop stickers and
  Polaroid frames over an image.
- A set of toggleable “themes” – neon 90s, grunge, VHS static – that recolor the
  site elements.

Basically anything that would’ve been a widget on a MySpace page: music
players, hit counters, animated gifs, playful cursors and hidden surprises.
Add them as optional flags so they don’t interfere with the main experience
but give your visitors a bit of nostalgia/whimsy.
